resolutions.researcher_notes: Atmos Energy's own current APT page describes the system in the present tense as an active network: 'Atmos Pipeline-Texas is a regulated intrastate natural gas transmission pipeline network and storage company' providing ongoing transportation/storage services. Wikipedia's Atmos Energy article independently describes it, also present-tense, as 'an intrastate natural gas transmission pipeline network which is connected to three major Texas market centers at Waha, Carthage, and Katy.' Two distinct publishers agree the system is operating.

Atmos's own page: 'approximately 5,700 miles of transmission pipelines' carrying 'natural gas production.' Wikipedia: 'intrastate natural gas transmission pipeline network.' Both distinct publishers confirm natural gas.

A Nov. 28, 2018 Vaquero Midstream investor/conference presentation (PDF, text layer extracted with pdftotext -layout -- confirmed by direct read, not an automated substring hit) diagrams Vaquero's tailgate interconnects and labels one: 'Atmos Line X-2 16" ... 180,000 Mcfd ... Bi-directional', i.e. 180 MMcf/d on an Atmos Pipeline-Texas interconnect -- an exact match to the sheet's Capacity=180.00 MMcf/d. NOTE: this figure traces to one specific interconnect/lateral (Atmos Line X-2) rather than the whole ~5,700-mile APT network's aggregate throughput; it is the same source gem.wiki's own [3] footnote traces to for this same number (read for lead purposes only, not cited). Only one publisher carries this specific number, so medium/independent=false; no second, independent source for 180 MMcf/d was found.

Atmos's own current page: 'approximately 5,700 miles of transmission pipelines within the state of Texas' -- exact match to sheet's LengthKnown=5700.00 mi. NOTE (not a CONCERN): Wikipedia's Atmos Energy article gives a different, larger approximate figure ('approximately 6,000 miles of transmission pipelines'), evidently a rounder/older count from a secondary encyclopedia rather than the company's own current figure; not used as corroboration here since it doesn't match the sheet's precise number. Only Atmos's own page carries the exact 5,700 mi figure, so medium/single-source.

Atmos's own page: the system runs 'within the state of Texas' and connects to 'production areas in central, north, west and east Texas' -- a Texas-to-Texas intrastate network, matching sheet's Start/End State=Texas. Wikipedia independently names the system's three major Texas market centers (Waha, Carthage, Katy), all in Texas. Two distinct publishers.

The 'About Atmos Pipeline-Texas' page is hosted on Atmos Energy's own corporate site (atmosenergy.com) and describes APT as Atmos's pipeline/storage business. Wikipedia's Atmos Energy article independently states this pipeline infrastructure is 'part of Atmos Energy's non-utility operations,' i.e. wholly Atmos's. Both corroborate Owner1='Atmos Energy Corp', Owner1%=100.00%. Two distinct publishers.
